$schema-note: Cross-runtime pin for the nst/JSONTestSuite (RFC 8259) corpus vendored at
test/JSONTestSuite/. Read by BOTH ts/test/jsontestsuite.test.ts and
go/jsontestsuite_test.go, so a TS/Go divergence on any pinned case shows
up as a failure in one runtime rather than as silence.
This is NOT a skip list. Every entry is a case where jsonc DELIBERATELY
diverges from strict RFC 8259, with the reason written down. The sets are
pinned EXACTLY: the tests fail if a lenience is gained OR lost. Update an
entry only together with the behaviour change that justifies it; never
re-pin to silence a red run.
`comments` and `trailingComma` are ADDITIONAL to `strict` — each mode's
allowlist is the union of the modes at or below it:

strict.n_number_+1.json: jsonic accepts a leading `+` on a number; RFC 8259 does not.
strict.n_number_-01.json: jsonic accepts a leading zero after the sign (`-01`); RFC 8259 does not.
strict.n_number_-2..json: jsonic accepts a trailing `.` with no fractional digits (`-2.`).
strict.n_number_0.e1.json: jsonic accepts an empty fraction before the exponent (`0.e1`).
strict.n_number_2.e+3.json: jsonic accepts `.` immediately before the exponent (`2.e+3`).
strict.n_number_2.e-3.json: jsonic accepts `.` immediately before the exponent (`2.e-3`).
strict.n_number_2.e3.json: jsonic accepts `.` immediately before the exponent (`2.e3`).
strict.n_number_neg_int_starting_with_zero.json: jsonic accepts a leading zero on a negative integer.
strict.n_number_neg_real_without_int_part.json: jsonic accepts a number with no integer part (`-.123`).
strict.n_number_real_without_fractional_part.js: jsonic accepts a trailing `.` with no fractional digits.
strict.n_number_with_leading_zero.json: jsonic accepts a leading zero on a positive integer.
strict.n_object_non_string_key.json: jsonic allows unquoted and non-string map keys; RFC 8259 requires strings.
strict.n_object_non_string_key_but_huge_number_: jsonic allows a numeric map key (`{9999E9999:1}`).
strict.n_object_repeated_null_null.json: jsonic allows the bare word `null` as a map key.
strict.n_single_space.json: Whitespace-only input resolves to `undefined` via the grammar's `#ZZ` alt on val.open rather than erroring.

comments.n_object_trailing_comment.json: Invalid JSON only because the document ends with a comment, which is legal JSONC.
comments.n_object_trailing_comment_slash_open.jso: Invalid JSON only because the document ends with an empty `//` comment, which is legal JSONC.
comments.n_structure_object_with_comment.json: Invalid JSON only because the object contains a `/* */` comment, which is legal JSONC.

trailingComma.n_array_extra_comma.json: Invalid JSON only because of a trailing comma in an array (`["",]`), legal under allowTrailingComma.
trailingComma.n_array_number_and_comma.json: Invalid JSON only because of a trailing comma in an array (`[1,]`), legal under allowTrailingComma.
trailingComma.n_object_lone_continuation_byte_in_key_a: Invalid JSON only because of a trailing comma in an object; the lone continuation byte in the key is accepted as text.
trailingComma.n_object_trailing_comma.json: Invalid JSON only because of a trailing comma in an object, legal under allowTrailingComma.

implementationDefinedAccepted-note: RFC 8259 leaves the i_* cases to the implementation, so neither verdict is
wrong — but an UNRECORDED verdict is. This is the exact set of i_* files
jsonc accepts, identical in all three option modes and in both runtimes.
The complement (the four UTF-16 / BOM-encoded documents) is rejected.
Pinned as a set so a change of behaviour on any single file is visible.
